job.title: Executive Assistant
job.description:
Two hundred emails a day, a flight most months, and nobody to share the load. Until now.

Angle Recruitment has partnered with an established marine engineering company, with teams across Asia, to find an Executive Assistant for one of its senior leaders.

The role is based in the west of Singapore, in a newly refurbished office near amenities, with affordable parking.

In short, your job is to give a busy senior leader his time back.

  • Take ownership of a heavy inbox, prioritising, filtering and replying on his behalf
  • Handle client and partner correspondence with the polish senior relationships deserve
  • Keep things running smoothly while he travels overseas each month
  • Look after personal matters and out of office commitments with discretion

You'll bring experience as an Executive Assistant or PA to senior leaders, and a legal or finance background would be a real advantage. You'll write well, think ahead and be trusted with confidential matters. Above all, you'll have the presence to hold your own with senior clients and internal staff alike while staying genuine and warm, and the judgement to know what needs escalating and what doesn't.

In return, you'll get a close working relationship with the leadership of a well established business, real influence over how it runs day to day, and a competitive package.

job.title: Head of Trade
job.description:
Angle Recruitment has partnered with an established shipping company to appoint its next Head of Trade.

Based in Singapore, you'll lead the trade and commercial strategy across key international markets, with responsibility for growth, profitability and execution.

  • Set and deliver the trade and commercial strategy
  • Drive pricing, yield, forecasting, capacity and P&L performance
  • Develop new commercial opportunities and strengthen existing trade performance
  • Manage key relationships with terminals, vendors, agents and partners
  • Work closely with Sales, Network, Operations, Procurement and Finance
  • Lead and develop a high-performing team

You'll bring senior commercial or trade experience in shipping, ideally from a carrier, with strong knowledge of international trade markets and a track record across pricing, yield, P&L and commercial strategy.

You'll be commercially driven, analytical and hands-on, with the ability to influence senior stakeholders and turn strategy into results.

job.title: Senior Chartering Manager, Chemical
job.description:
Established chemical tanker fleet needs someone to keep it fixed and earning.

Angle Recruitment has partnered with an international shipping company in the chemical tanker market. The fleet is growing fast, with newbuilds delivering through 2027 and more tonnage chartered in alongside.

The role is based in Singapore, working closely with the head of the commercial team and alongside established chartering colleagues.

In short, your job is to fix stainless steel chemical tankers profitably, mostly in Asia, with the chance to fix globally and learn new ports and trades.

  • Fix the fleet on spot and contract business, mainly intra Asia with deep sea trades too
  • Build and look after relationships with charterers, traders and brokers
  • Spot cargo opportunities and position vessels to get the best voyage results
  • Work closely with operations so fixtures run smoothly from negotiation to discharge
  • Help bring new vessels into the market as the fleet expands


You'll bring chartering experience on stainless steel chemical tankers, including deep sea fixing. You'll need to be based in Singapore or willing to relocate here.

In return, you'll get a real voice in a fleet that is growing quickly, a commercial team that moves fast, and a strong package to match.

job.title: Technical Director, Ship Management
job.description:
Technical Director, In-House Ship Management - Germany

Build an in-house ship management operation from scratch, then run it.

Angle Recruitment has partnered exclusively with a growing international shipowner that is building its own in-house ship management, so it is no longer solely reliant on third party managers. You'll be based in Germany and report directly to the board.

As Head of In-House Ship Management, you'll own the whole function for the owner's growing fleet, including its OPEX and CAPEX. That covers technical, newbuilding, marine and HSEQ, procurement and crewing. In the first six months you'll start small, decide what sits in-house and what's outsourced, and put in place the structure, systems and people the business needs to scale.

  • Set up the in-house organisation, its systems and the DOC, ISM, ISPS and SMS framework
  • Build and lead a team across technical and marine superintendency, QHSE, DPA, procurement and crewing
  • Take vessels over from third party managers, lead technical due diligence on acquisitions and oversee newbuilding projects
  • Own the OPEX and CAPEX budgets, planned maintenance, dry dockings and special surveys
  • Build a strong safety culture, and relationships with class, flag, yards, suppliers and crewing partners


You'll bring significant shore based experience running ship management for an owner or third party manager. You'll know ISM, ISPS, SOLAS and MARPOL inside out. You'll have handled takeovers, dockings and budgets, and you keep a firm grip on costs. Fluent English is essential.

A seagoing background as Master would be an advantage, or Chief Engineer with substantial fleet management experience. So would experience with specialised tonnage or newbuildings, or having set up a ship management organisation before. German is useful but not required.

In return, you'll get the rare chance to build an owner's ship management operation rather than inherit one. You'll have real autonomy, a seat at the centre of the group's maritime leadership and a package to match.

job.title: Vessel Operator - Dry Bulk
job.description:
A well-backed dry bulk operator is expanding its Singapore office and is looking for an experienced Operations Executive to independently manage vessels across Pacific trade lanes.

The company currently operates a growing fleet of Handysize & Handymax vessels under long-term time charters, with further deliveries scheduled next year and a clear growth path toward a substantially larger fleet over the next few years. The model is pure operator for now, with plans to acquire tonnage in the future.

The Role

  • Independently run day-to-day operations for allocated vessels and Pacific trade lanes
  • Coordinate closely with the chartering team and owners
  • Handle commercial operations, including occasional parceling
  • Support the broader operation, including occasional assistance on Atlantic cargo
  • Work closely with the existing operations team based in Europe

Requirements

  • Solid experience with Handy and Ultramax tonnage (ideally from an operator background)
  • Strong Chinese (Mandarin) language skills
  • Comfortable working in the office five days per week
  • 7–8 years’ relevant experience preferred; open to candidates from both operator and EP backgrounds

This is a hands-on role with real ownership and visibility in a growing organisation. Apply now!

job.title: Global Head of Crewing, Ship Owner
job.description:
Take over a well run crewing operation and shape where it goes next.

Angle Recruitment has partnered with a major international shipowner to appoint its Global Head of Crewing. The group runs a mixed merchant fleet of vessels and is raising the bar on crew quality, vetting and commercial focus.

The role is based in London, with the fleet crewed through owned and third party manning offices.

In short, your job is to set the crew strategy for the fleet and see it delivered on every ship.

  • Lead crew strategy, planning and budgets for the fleet
  • Build the crew pool and succession planning for the top four ranks
  • Keep manning in line with charterer, RightShip, DBMS and flag requirements
  • Drive performance management with Masters, Chief Engineers and the manning offices
  • Lead a team of crew operators and coordinators

You'll bring leadership experience within crewing for an owner or manager, and you must have managed crewing for a fleet of at least double figures. Seagoing experience is welcome but not essential. You'll know RightShip, DBMS, MLC and collective bargaining agreements well, communicate clearly, solve problems with a sense of urgency and care about the people at sea.

In return, you'll get a senior seat in a respected international shipping group, private medical for your family from day one, and visa and relocation support for the right person.

job.title: Head of Marine and Vetting, Ship Owner
job.description:
Own marine standards and vetting across a mixed merchant fleet.

Angle Recruitment has partnered with a major international shipowner to appoint its Head of Marine and Vetting. The group operates a mixed merchant fleet of vessels, including wet and dry tonnage.

The role is based in London and leads a dedicated marine team working remotely.

In short, your job is to keep the fleet safe, compliant and approved by the majors and charterers.

  • Lead marine operations across navigation, cargo and incident management
  • Own vetting performance and oil major approvals across the tanker fleet
  • Lead and develop a remote marine team
  • Take on DPA responsibilities or a similar function
  • Build strong relationships with charterers, terminals and the majors

You'll bring senior experience in both marine operations and vetting across wet and dry tonnage, and you must have both. Time as DPA or in a similar role is ideal. You'll have managed remote teams, have a strong network across the industry and be a clear communicator.

In return, you'll get a senior role with real authority in a respected international shipping group.

job.title: Commercial Operations Manager, Shipping Alternative Fuels (Ammonia)
job.description:
中文职位描述请见下方

Ammonia is moving from cargo to fuel, and this role sits right in the middle of it.

Angle Recruitment has partnered with a global international shipowner that is investing heavily in low carbon fuels and building the vessels to burn them. It is now growing its operations team in Asia.

The role is based in Singapore, covering Asia Pacific, with close links to the group's partners across the Far East.

Fluent English and Chinese (Mandarin), spoken and written, are essential for this role. Applications without both can't be considered.

In short, your job is to keep the ammonia voyages running well and make sure the commercial side gets the numbers it needs.

  • Support the chartering team on fixtures, bringing a solid read of the ammonia shipping market
  • Run voyages day to day with charterers, brokers, agents and technical managers
  • Oversee loading, discharge, cargo operations and ammonia bunkering, in line with contracts and safety requirements
  • Be the main point of contact, working in Chinese, for the group's partners in the region on bunkering, trading and operational matters
  • Report trading and operational performance to senior management

You'll be familiar with ammonia shipping, ideally on the bunkering side, though given how niche and specialised the role is, cargo experience will also be considered. You'll be fluent in English and Chinese, both spoken and written, and bring sharp commercial sense and an easy way of working across cultures. A degree in business, economics or trade is expected, and a maritime or chemical background helps.

In return, you'll report directly into senior leadership at a business that's genuinely shaping how shipping decarbonises, with a remuneration package to match.


商务运营经理，航运替代燃料（氨）

氨正在从货物转变为燃料，而这个职位正处于这一转变的核心。

Angle Recruitment 现与一家全球性国际船东合作。该公司正大力投资低碳燃料，并建造使用这些燃料的船舶，目前正在扩充其亚洲运营团队。

该职位常驻新加坡，负责亚太区，并与集团在远东地区的合作伙伴保持紧密联系。

本职位要求流利的英语和中文（普通话），包括口语和书面表达。不同时具备两种语言能力的申请将不予考虑。

简而言之，您的工作是确保氨运输航次顺利运行，并为商务团队提供所需的数据。

  • 支持租船团队完成租船成交，提供对氨运输市场的深入了解
  • 与租家、经纪人、代理和技术管理方合作，负责航次的日常运营
  • 根据合同和安全要求，监督装货、卸货、货物操作及氨燃料加注
  • 作为集团在本地区合作伙伴的主要联络人，以中文沟通燃料加注、贸易及运营事宜
  • 向高级管理层汇报贸易和运营业绩

您需熟悉氨运输业务，最好具备燃料加注方面的经验；鉴于该职位专业性强、人才稀缺，具备货运经验者也将被考虑。您需具备流利的英语和中文口语及书面能力，拥有敏锐的商业意识，并能在多元文化环境中顺畅合作。应具备商科、经济或贸易相关学位，具有航运或化工背景者优先。

作为回报，您将直接向高级领导层汇报，加入一家真正推动航运业脱碳进程的企业，并获得与职位相匹配的薪酬待遇。

job.title: Executive Search Researcher
job.description:
Find the people nobody else can, then find out what makes them tick.

Angle Recruitment is a Singapore based maritime search firm placing shore based leaders across shipping, offshore, energy and commodities.

Retained search is a large part of our business, led by our Managing Director, who you'll work very closely with. He has 15 years in maritime executive search, spanning C-suite, Board and Non-Executive Director appointments, and he's keen to teach it. More on us, and him, here: https://www.anglerecruitment.com/about-us

The role is based in our Paya Lebar office, covering senior searches across Asia, the Middle East and Europe. For the right person, we'd consider remote working from another country.

Fluent written and spoken Chinese is essential.

In short, your job is to map the market so thoroughly that when we present a shortlist, the client knows there's nobody we missed.

  • Build market maps and target company lists for each search
  • Identify, approach and qualify candidates, many of whom aren't looking
  • Run first conversations and turn them into clear, concise candidate notes
  • Keep our research and candidate records accurate in JobAdder
  • Track who's moving where across the maritime sector

You'll bring at least two years in executive search research, talent mapping or a similar sourcing role. Fluent written and spoken Chinese is essential. You don't need maritime or energy experience, we teach all of that, and our training is excellent.

Above all, you'll be confident asking executives the difficult questions, curious enough to probe when something doesn't add up, and business minded enough to connect the dots on where the opportunities lie. You'll handle sensitive feedback with tact, and you'll be the kind of person others warm to quickly and come to value.

In return, you'll get close exposure to senior international searches, a small team where your work is seen, and a clear pathway to becoming the best researcher in maritime.

job.title: Business Development Engineer, Asia-Pacific
job.description:
An engineering company at heart, a first mover OEM by nature. They have spent years leading on marine technology, and competitors are still catching up.

Angle Recruitment has partnered exclusively with a high end international marine engineering business. It runs a serious R&D engine, and its equipment is trusted on premium leisure, passenger, offshore and naval vessels worldwide. The Asia-Pacific business is established and ready to scale, and this hire sits at the heart of that.

The role
You will sell to shipyards across Asia-Pacific, opening new accounts and growing the ones already on the books. Orders typically run from $50k to $1m. Commercial enough to win the order, technical enough to support the project through to start up and commissioning, and troubleshoot when needed.

This is a remote role with plenty of travel across the region, including mainland China and Taiwan, plus occasional trips to Europe and the US. Singapore, Hong Kong or China all work as a base. You will report to the Managing Director.

What you bring

  • Sales or business development experience in marine or industrial equipment, selling into shipyards
  • A genuinely technical background, with the confidence to hold your own with a yard's engineering and project teams and support start ups on board
  • Strong communication skills, in front of a yard owner or a commissioning crew
  • Existing relationships with newbuilding yards in Asia
  • Freedom to travel across the whole region, including China and Taiwan, and to hold a long term US visa
  • Chinese language skills will be a real advantage


Why it's worth a conversation

  • A high end, niche product with no Asian manufacturer competing
  • A real hand in accelerating growth across Asia-Pacific
  • Privately owned and engineering led
  • Remote working with the freedom to run your own region
  • Competitive salary and rewarding bonus

job.title: Technical Advisor
job.description:
Adventure, travel and science, with the ocean as your client.

Angle Recruitment has partnered with a respected not for profit organisation, funded by the shipping industry, to find a Technical Advisor. When oil or chemicals are spilt at sea, this is the team governments, shipowners, insurers and salvors call for impartial technical advice.

The role is based in Singapore or the UK, part of a global group of specialists. When an incident happens, big or small, you'll be on a plane and at the heart of the action, on site for up to three weeks at a time.

  • Lead cases and advise on the best response to oil and chemical spills
  • Attend incidents on site across Asia Pacific, Africa and beyond
  • Work alongside governments, owners, insurers and salvors to keep the response on track
  • Write reports, deliver presentations and training, and represent the organisation with industry and government


You'll bring a Master's degree or PhD in a natural science, most likely chemistry, marine biology, oceanography or environmental science. Spill response, port chemistry or marine environmental experience may help. Another language besides English would be useful, but isn't essential.

Above all, you'll be able to explain complex science to people who have none.

Between incidents the pace is steadier, so strong writing and calm judgement matter as much as a willingness to travel at short notice.

In return, you'll get a structured induction, a mentor from the senior team and genuinely meaningful work with global reach.

job.title: Newbuild Project Manager, OCV
job.description:
Offshore construction vessels are some of the most complex ships afloat. This role puts you in charge of building them.

Angle Recruitment has partnered with a reputable offshore and renewables company. A series of offshore construction vessels is on order, and this hire will see them through the yard.

The role is based in Singapore, mainly in the office, with regular trips to shipyards in Asia.

In short, your job is to turn a specification into vessels that are ready to go to work.

  • Manage OCV newbuild projects from design approval through commissioning, sea trials and delivery
  • Work with the site team and the yard's technical and commercial teams to keep schedule, cost and quality on track
  • Take the lead on electrical, power and automation systems, from DP and power management to mission equipment integration
  • Handle variation orders, inspections, FATs and outstanding items, bringing in class, flag and makers when needed
  • Report progress and risk clearly, and flag problems early

You'll have worked on the owner's side of pipelay, cablelay or CSOV vessels, at sea or ashore. An electrical background is ideal, though a marine engineering or academic route into the industry works too. Newbuild or conversion experience will put you ahead.

In return, you'll get a newbuild programme you can shape from the start, a business with room to grow, and a package to match the role.

job.title: Head of Operations | Chemical Vessels
job.description:
Keep the fleet moving, the tanks clean and the charterers happy.

Angle Recruitment has partnered with a reputable shipping company to find its next Head of Operations. The company operates a fleet of IMO Type 1 and 2 chemical tankers trading globally.

The role is based in Singapore, leading commercial operations across the whole fleet.

In short, your job is to make every voyage run safely, on time and on budget, with tank cleaning that never costs the next fixture.

  • Lead post fixture operations, from voyage instructions through to cargo handling and performance
  • Own tank cleaning and cargo planning across stainless steel tank vessels
  • Work closely with chartering, technical and vetting to keep the fleet earning
  • Handle the difficult moments: deviations, off hire, claims and cargo disputes
  • Build and lead the operations team


You'll bring solid experience operating IMO Type 1 and 2 chemical tankers with stainless steel tanks, and a working knowledge of tank cleaning that only comes from doing it. You'll have operated vessels into global ports, with the Middle East, Europe or the Americas an advantage. A seagoing background will help, but it isn't essential.

In return, you'll get a senior role with a respected owner, real influence over how the fleet performs, and a remuneration package to match

job.title: Newbuild Project Manager, LNGC
job.description:
Take an LNG carrier from steel cutting to delivery, and be the company's voice at the yard while you do it.

Angle Recruitment has partnered with a reputable shipping company with a modern fleet across gas carriers and offshore. Its newbuilding programme is under way, and this hire leads the LNG side of it.

The role is based in Singapore, with regular time on site at the shipyard.

In short, your job is to get the vessels delivered on time, on budget and to spec.

  • Run LNG carrier newbuilding projects from design and construction through commissioning, sea trials and delivery
  • Represent the company with the yard, class, designers and makers, keeping a firm grip on quality, schedule and cost
  • Review specifications, drawings and systems, from cargo containment and handling to propulsion and automation
  • Manage inspections, FATs, modifications and defects, and lead the site team
  • Report progress and risk, and keep everything compliant with the IGC Code, IMO, class and flag

You'll have sailed as an engineer on LNG carriers, and bring at least eight years in newbuilding. You'll have worked as a site superintendent, a newbuild project manager or on the yard side, and have taken vessels through commissioning, sea trials and delivery. Above all, you'll hold your own with a shipyard.

In return, you'll get the chance to shape an LNG newbuild programme from the start, a business with room to grow, and a package to match the role.

job.title: Sales Manager, Marine Environmental Technology (China)
job.description:
Get in front of the yards, know the competition better than they know themselves, and win the business.

Angle Recruitment has partnered with a well regarded European maritime technology group to find a Sales Manager for China. The group's portfolio spans decarbonisation, water treatment, and environmental marine equipment, with tens of thousands of systems in service across the world fleet.

The role is field based and covers shipyards and owners across China, so expect plenty of time on the road. It's one of several new sales hires as the group strengthens its commercial team worldwide.

In short, you'll open doors and close orders.

  • Build and deliver your own business development plan for China
  • Present the group's systems at shipyards across the major building regions, for newbuilds and retrofits
  • Win orders against established domestic and international competitors
  • Keep a healthy pipeline and work closely with group sales leadership in Europe
  • Represent the business at exhibitions and industry events, including Marintec

You'll bring a track record selling marine equipment or systems into Chinese shipyards, ideally in environmental, water treatment or decarbonisation technology. You'll have strong yard relationships and be out in the field rather than behind a desk. You'll also have fluent Mandarin and good business English for working with a European head office.

In return, you'll get a strong product range behind you, a group investing in growth and a direct line to senior leadership. There's also a competitive package of base salary, target linked bonus and a generous monthly allowance.

job.title: Sales Manager, Marine Environmental Technology (Singapore)
job.description:
Get in front of the yards, know the competition better than they know themselves, and win the business.

Angle Recruitment has partnered with a well regarded European maritime technology group to find a Sales Manager for Singapore. The group's portfolio spans decarbonisation, water treatment, and environmental marine equipment, with tens of thousands of systems in service across the world fleet.

The role is based in Singapore, covering shipyards, owners and managers across the region. It's one of several new sales hires as the group strengthens its commercial team worldwide.

In short, you'll open doors and close orders.

  • Build and deliver your own business development plan for the region
  • Present the group's systems to shipyards, owners and ship managers, for newbuilds and retrofits
  • Win orders against established competitors, with a sharp read on who's quoting what
  • Keep a healthy pipeline and work closely with group sales leadership in Europe
  • Represent the business at exhibitions and industry events

You'll bring a track record selling marine equipment or systems into shipyards and shipowners, ideally in environmental, water treatment or decarbonisation technology. You'll be out in the field rather than behind a desk, comfortable working with a European head office, and hungry to build something. Mandarin would be a strong advantage given the yard base in China.

In return, you'll get a proven product range, a group investing in growth and a direct line to senior leadership. There's also a competitive package of base salary plus a target linked bonus.

job.title: Senior Technical Superintendent, Drybulk (MPP)
job.description:
Keep the bulkers in class, on budget and earning.

Angle Recruitment has partnered with a renowned ship owner/operator to find a Senior Technical Superintendent (Dry Bulk) for its Singapore office. The company operates a dry bulk fleet and runs its technical management with real care for the ships and the people on them.

The role is based in Singapore, with regular travel across the region for attendances, dry dockings and inspections.

In short, your job is to keep your vessels safe, compliant and trading without interruption.

  • Take full technical responsibility for a group of dry bulk vessels
  • Plan and supervise dry dockings, repairs and special surveys
  • Manage vessel budgets, spares and maintenance planning
  • Handle PSC, vetting and class matters, and close out findings promptly
  • Support and guide the senior officers on board and junior superintendents ashore

You'll bring proven experience as a Technical Superintendent and hands on dry bulk experience, whether ashore or at sea. Experience with geared bulkers, cranes and grabs will be well-regarded. You'll also have the judgement to make sound calls under pressure and the presence to hold your own with yards, class and owners alike.

In return, you'll join a well regarded owner/operator with a long term view of its fleet, a strong team around you and a remuneration package to match the role.

job.title: Senior Manager, Chartering & Business Development
job.description:
Angle is supporting an established ship operator to hire a Senior Chartering Manager. This person will build and lead the long-term time charter book. This role offers a path to grow into more senior leadership roles as the business develops.

You’ll originate and develop relationships with cargo owners and charterers, long-term time charters, this will be your predominant focus. Grow a stable cargo base that supports geared and gearless fleet. Alongside the longer-term development work, you’ll also run profitable day-to-day chartering, matching cargoes and vessels, negotiating fixtures, and taking controlled positions on third-party tonnage within approved limits.

This is an individual contributor role reporting to the Head of Drybulk. You’ll work closely with Operations, Finance, Risk and Post Fixture internally, and with shipowners, charterers, brokers and agents externally. Success will be measured by the pipeline of strategic accounts and long-term opportunities you build, the COAs and long-term contracts you convert, and the commercial returns you deliver. Those who perform will have the opportunity to step into broader leadership responsibilities as the platform grows.

What you bring

  • Significant drybulk chartering experience, ideally across more than one side of the market.
  • A proven record of winning new business, particularly COAs or long-term time charters
  • Strong market sense and an established network among cargo owners, charterers and brokers
  • The ability to negotiate confidently and build relationships at every level


If you’ve built long-term business before and want to do it again from a relatively small starting point, with room to grow into leadership, we’d like to hear from you.

job.title: Marine Sales Manager
job.description:
Marine Sales Manager

Angle Recruitment is currently supporting the International Marine Solution company to find a Marine Sales Manager who will lead the sales function, driving revenue growth, customer development and market expansion across the maritime sector.
This role requires a commercially focused leader who can develop and execute effective sales strategies, manage and develop the sales team, strengthen key customer relationships and identify new business opportunities. The successful candidate will work closely with Management and internal teams to ensure sustainable growth and profitability.

Sales Leadership & Strategy

  • Lead, manage and develop the Sales team to achieve revenue and business targets.
  • Develop and execute sales strategies aligned with the company's overall business objectives.
  • Monitor team performance and implement improvement plans where required.
  • Prepare sales forecasts, performance reports and market updates for Management.
  • Build a collaborative, accountable and high-performing sales culture.

Business Development & Customer Management

  • Develop and maintain strong relationships with key maritime customers and strategic accounts.
  • Identify and develop new business opportunities across the marine sector.
  • Understand customer requirements and provide suitable commercial and technical solutions in collaboration with internal teams.
  • Attend client meetings, maritime exhibitions, conferences and industry events to develop market presence and new opportunities.
  • Build and maintain a strong sales pipeline across existing and prospective customers.

Commercial Growth & Market Development

  • Lead commercial negotiations and support contracts through to successful closure.
  • Monitor vessel movements, fleet activities and customer developments to identify sales opportunities.
  • Analyse market trends, competitor activity and customer behaviour, providing relevant insights to Management.
  • Develop strategies to improve performance across underperforming territories, customer segments and product/service categories.
  • Ensure sales growth is commercially sustainable and aligned with profitability objectives.

Requirements

  • Diploma or Degree in Business, Marketing, Engineering or a related discipline.
  • Strong sales experience, with previous team management or leadership experience.
  • Experience within marine equipment, marine services or the wider maritime industry would be highly advantageous.
  • Strong business development, strategic planning and market analysis capabilities.
  • Proven ability to develop customer relationships and manage commercial negotiations.
  • Strong leadership and people-development skills.
  • Excellent communication, negotiation and presentation abilities.
  • Proficient in MS Office and CRM systems.
  • Self-motivated, commercially minded and able to work independently.
  • Strong organisational skills with the ability to manage multiple priorities.
  • Willingness to travel overseas when required.

job.title: Vessel Manager (Heavy-Lift & Project Cargo)
job.description:
Our client is an established shipping company with a long record in heavy lift and project cargo, moving the awkward and the oversized worldwide: wind turbine components, transformers, modules and marine equipment.

Technical management sits in Singapore, close to the commercial desk, so this is a role where the superintendent is part of the conversation on what the ships can lift, not just who keeps them running.

The role

  • You'll own a small fleet of heavy lift vessels end to end: maintenance, drydocking, budgets, crew and compliance.
  • You'll review lift plans, ballast and stability calculations and sea fastening with the cargo engineers, attend critical lifts, and keep the cranes, wires and hydraulics to class and maker standard.
  • You'll prepare vessels for charterer vetting, close out audits, manage OPEX and drydock budgets, and build a proper working relationship with your Masters and Chief Engineers.
  • Some travel, sometimes at short notice.


You

  • You're already a Vessel Manager or Technical Superintendent.
  • Heavy lift, project cargo or offshore construction vessels are a must.
  • You know your way around heavy lift cranes (Liebherr, NMF, Huisman or similar), ISM, class and PMS, and you're comfortable reading a lift plan.
  • Hands on, calm under pressure and commercially aware.

job.title: Head of Crewing
job.description:
One of Papua New Guinea’s largest shipowners is seeking an experienced Head of Crewing to lead crewing operations from their Lae office.

About the Company The company operates a fleet of 25+ vessels, including tugs, barges, smaller container ships, tankers and dry bulk carriers. This is a substantial, established owner (not an agency) with a significant presence in the Pacific. The role is a genuine long-term leadership position — the current incumbent is on a contractor/seafarer contract, and the company now wants a permanent Head of Crewing who will fully own the function.

The Role You will report to the General Manager (based in Port Moresby) and lead a team of six. You will be responsible for a pool of around 600 crew drawn from Papua New Guinea, Philippines, India, China, Malaysia and other nationalities.

This is an office-based role in a 24/7 operational environment. Secure transport is provided between accommodation and the workplace.

Key Requirements

  • Deep, hands-on knowledge of crewing — particularly rostering, crew planning and training
  • Proven experience leading and managing a crewing team
  • Comfortable operating in a high-tempo, 24/7 maritime environment
  • Strong organisational and stakeholder management skills
  • Previous experience with multi-national crew pools is highly advantageous

What's on Offer

  • Visa support
  • Club memberships
  • High-quality accommodation within a secure compound
  • Secure transport

This is one of the more substantial crewing leadership roles currently available in the Pacific. The company has a track record of supporting international hires and provides a secure, well-managed living environment.

To apply or discuss the role further, please reply with your CV and a brief outline of your relevant crewing leadership experience. All applications will be treated in strict confidence.

job.title: Vessel Operator, Product Tankers
job.description:
Keep the ships moving, the ports honest and the voyage result where it should be.

Our client is a well regarded international shipping company in the tanker space, moving chemicals and clean petroleum products across Asia Pacific, the Americas and Europe. Its Singapore office runs a mix of controlled tonnage, COAs and spot fixtures.

They are adding a Vessel Operator to the Pacific operations team. It's a small team that shares knowledge, reporting to the Operations Manager, with the occasional port or vessel visit.

In short, you will run the daily operation of an assigned fleet as efficiently and economically as possible.

  • Issue voyage instructions, monitor bunkers, drafts and ETAs, and maximise cargo intake at load ports
  • Nominate agents, review pro formas and DAs, and challenge any lost time in port
  • Track off hire, support demurrage and laytime claims, and check freight invoices
  • Prepare voyage estimates and keep IMOS voyage files clean, current and handed over properly
  • Oversee tank cleaning with owners and managers, and maintain vessel and port KPIs


You will be a well versed tanker operator, ideally from chemicals or CPP, with a sound grasp of time charter, COA and voyage charter terms. You know how ships, ports and terminals work, you understand tank cleaning and cargo handling, and you can negotiate firmly without falling out with anyone. IMOS experience is a plus. Sailing experience would also help, but it isn't required. The trade runs around the clock, so you will need to be comfortable taking a call outside office hours.

In return, you join a respected name with strong backing, a steady fleet and a team that invests in its people. A competitive package is on offer for the right person.

job.title: Environmental Data Specialist (Shipping)
job.description:
Angle Recruitment has partnered with a well established shipping company to find an Environmental Data Specialist who can bring order to how it measures and reports its impact.

Like every shipowner, the business has to report its carbon emissions, waste and water use. It burns fuel at sea, uses electricity ashore, sends crew and staff around the world, and buys goods and services from hundreds of suppliers. The rules for reporting all this are clear. The data behind it is not. Some figures come from systems, some from spreadsheets, and some from a vessel emailing numbers to the office. Each office does it a little differently, so the totals are hard to trust.

Your job is to fix that, and make sure it stays fixed.

You'll sit in Finance, reporting to the Finance Controller, because the priority is numbers that stand up to an auditor. You'll work closely with a small sustainability team of four, two on the fleet side and two in corporate, who know the business and the targets.

In practice, you will:

  • Set the rules. Turn group data policy into a practical way of working, with clear owners, controls and the evidence an auditor will ask for.
  • Find the gaps. Map where every piece of carbon, waste and water data comes from, and spot the duplication, risks and manual workarounds.
  • Check the numbers. Test data from across the business, spot what doesn't add up, and explain why.
  • Deliver the tools. Build the case for practical tools and automation, then implement them within the systems that exist today.
  • Crack Scope 3. Build a sensible approach to supplier, travel and crewing data, including business travel emissions and offsetting.
  • Make it stick. Write clear guides and train the people who supply the data, so the process runs long after the two years are up.


You'll bring hands on experience managing Scope 1 and 2 inventories under the GHG Protocol, and a good eye for whether data is clean. You'll have designed data processes and controls that held up to review, ideally with some exposure to Scope 3 and external assurance. Shipping knowledge is useful but not essential. The client is open to someone slightly earlier in their career, as long as the carbon accounting and data quality skills are genuinely there.

In return, you'll get a clear brief, real influence across the business, and a competitive package. It's two years to build something that lasts.
